description: The Lunar Navigators is a Chennai-based team competing in the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. We build interactive WebGL software that processes NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data to evaluate candidate landing sites on the Moon. Our project calculates surface slope, solar illumination, and direct-to-Earth communication availability in real time, giving mission planners a functional, browser-based tool to compare landing zones.
summary: The Lunar South Pole Mission Evaluator is a production-grade lunar mission-planning dashboard engineered to solve critical landing site selection challenges for NASA's Artemis program. Addressing the strict illumination and communication constraints of the lunar South Pole, the application leverages verified NASA JPL DE441 ephemerides in the MEAN_ME coordinate frame to provide high-precision 30-day trade studies. Users can analyze solar power availability and Earth direct-to-earth (DTE) communications across key candidate sites like Shackleton and Haworth craters or evaluate custom coordinates with a robust analytical fallback. By combining a tactical NASA flight-console interface with interactive 3D WebGL topography and half-hour client-side interpolation, the tool bridges raw astrodynamic data with intuitive mission execution. It provides essential insights for maximizing surface operational efficiency and continuous power collection near permanently shadowed regions (PSRs).
details:
• What it does & how it works: The application is a web-based lunar mission-planning engine that evaluates solar power generation and Earth communication visibility for the lunar South Pole. It operates via a hybrid architecture: a static, high-performance public cache of verified hourly JPL DE441 topocentric ephemerides provides exact data for preset candidate sites, while an analytical Meeus/ELP-2000 fallback supports arbitrary custom coordinates. A client-side interpolation engine computes half-hour steps and handles azimuth wraparound, driven by an interactive 30-day timeline scrubber and synchronized 3D WebGL terrain views.
  • Benefits: It delivers sub-hourly navigational precision without runtime network bottlenecks, allowing mission planners to instantly cross-compare multi-site trade studies, identify ice-trap power constraints, and export structured CSV telemetry reports.
  • Intended Impact: To streamline preliminary lunar reconnaissance and site-feasibility assessments for space agencies, researchers, and student aerospace teams navigating the extreme topography and illumination geometries of the lunar South Pole.
    • Frontend & Logic: TypeScript, React, Vite.
    • 3D Graphics & Styling: Three.js (WebGL topography and lighting vectors), Tailwind CSS (custom tactical NASA JPL console design).
    • Data Ingestion & Processing: Python (automated NASA JPL Horizons REST API scraper with coordinate encoding and footnote sanitization).
    • Data Standards: JPL DE441 ephemerides, MEAN_ME coordinate frame, JSON.
  • Creativity: The project breaks away from generic dashboard templates by adopting an authentic aerospace flight-director aesthetic—utilizing matte obsidian surfaces, 1px tactical borders, aviation amber power indicators, and tabular monospace telemetry. It bridges heavy computational astrodynamics with lightweight, responsive browser execution.
    • Cross-Device Performance: Implemented WebGL pixel-ratio capping, context-loss handlers, and adaptive mesh segment density to prevent mobile crashes and ensure smooth rendering across devices.
    • Data Integrity: Maintained transparent labeling distinguishing verified JPL DE441 cache entries from analytical fallback models.
    • Performance Optimization: Decoupled the 720-hour ephemeris dataset into a static public asset with single-request deduplication on startup to maintain a lightweight core JS bundle.
